newsitem.title: UK: CE gets extension on announcement for bid.
newsitem.headline: CE gets extension on announcement for bid.

text.p: U.S.-based CE Electric said it had gained approval from UK takeover authorities to extend the deadline for an announcement on its 782 million stg bid for Northern Electric to 2400 GMT from 1700 GMT.
In a statement, the company said the Takeovers Panel had allowed the extension but gave no reason for the delay.
The 650 pence per share bid closed at 1300 GMT on Friday and analysts said it was in the balance whether regional electricity company (Rec) Northern would manage to retain its independence.
CE Electric, which is 70 percent owned by CalEnergy of the U.S., has bought nearly 30 percent of the company on the market and has declared acceptances for around four percent more.

It raised its bid from an original 630 pence per share on December 6 and had hoped to secure agreement from Northern, the only Rec to have fought off a predator when it spent 560 million stg to fend off Trafalgar House, now part of Kvaerner, last year.
If the bid is successful, it will leave just two of the original 12 cash-rich Recs independent, Yorkshire and Southern.
Three Recs have already been sold to American companies and agreed offers for two others -- East Midlands and London -- are underway.
